ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure gives several molecular structures, in which propane is shown as a hydrocarbon molecule with three carbon atoms connected, and ethene is shown as a hydrocarbon molecule with a double bond between two carbon atoms. Reasoning: propane and ethene are both hydrocarbons, and the main intermolecular forces are London dispersion forces. propane has three carbon atoms, and compared with ethene's two carbon atoms, it contains more total electrons, and its electron cloud is larger and more easily polarized. A more polarizable electron cloud will produce stronger instantaneous dipole-induced dipole attractions, so more energy is needed to separate the molecules and make them boil. Therefore the boiling point of propane is likely higher than that of ethene.
